answer: One defence is to make each identity pay a real, unforgeable cost before it can transact. A new agent must lock a refundable bond and complete a unique proof-of-work puzzle tied to its public key; the bond is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Like a single marble dropped into a lagoon, one fake identity barely ripples the market, but creating thousands requires proportional bonds and compute, so a Sybil flood becomes unaffordable, while honest newcomers in a sparse tundra of early adoption still face only a modest, recoverable cost.
